conventions.convention: H is the commutative polynomial algebra over Q on isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees. Forests are finite multisets, the empty forest is 1, and degree counts vertices.

Edges point from parent to child. An admissible edge cut meets each root-to-leaf path at most once. P is the child-side forest and R is the root-side component. The coproduct includes the empty edge cut and a separate virtual full cut above the root, retaining multiplicities of distinct edge subsets.
K is a commutative unital Q-algebra; epsilon is formal. Laurent series have finitely many negative powers. R retains strictly negative powers, so constants belong to A_+ and R(1)=0.

Characters are unital algebra homomorphisms H→A. Convolution uses the ordered coproduct factors, the counterterm recursion is phi_-(h)=-R B_phi(h), and phi_+=phi_-*phi; consequently phi=phi_-^{-1}*phi_+.
The construction is an abstract rooted-tree subtraction model; no graph-to-rooted-tree identification or physical realization is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Defines H=Q[T], the admissible-cut coproduct Δ(t)=t⊗1+Σ_C P_C(t)⊗R_C(t), its multiplicative extension to forests, and the counit killing nonempty forests.

The specified H is a connected graded bialgebra with a unique two-sided convolution inverse S of its identity map. S(1)=1 and S(t)=-t-Σ_C S(P_C(t))R_C(t), summing over nonempty admissible edge cuts; the recursion is finite and S is multiplicative on forests.

For a commutative unital Q-algebra K, A=K((epsilon)) splits as A_-⊕A_+, where A_- consists of finite sums of strictly negative powers and A_+ consists of formal nonnegative-power series; R projects onto A_-.
For a character phi:H→A, the finite degree recursion defines characters phi_- and phi_+=phi_-*phi with phi_-(H_+)⊆A_- and phi_+(H)⊆A_+. The inverse phi_-^{-1}=phi_-∘S exists and phi=phi_-^{-1}*phi_+.
